## Before class (the flip)

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.activity-card}
[Bring · 20 minutes at home]{.card-title}

1. **One A3 output**: a table, chart, map, or model result.
2. **Two diagram briefs** from your own project, written for someone else to draw. Use the brief format on the next slide.
3. Spend five minutes with the [Threshold Explorer](../site_tools/threshold-explorer.html). Move one slider until the recommendation changes.
:::

::: {.concept-card}
[In class, we do not lecture at you]{.card-title}

- **Session 1:** we look at drawn threshold diagrams and argue about where the lines are.
- **Session 2:** you draw each other's briefs three ways (hand, AI, data tool) and compare.
- Three of us: two students and the instructor. The instructor writes two briefs too and is drawn, judged, and challenged like everyone else.
:::
::::

---

## The brief you bring (×2)

Write it so a classmate who does not know your project could draw it.

| Field | What to write |
|---|---|
| **Decision** | the choice this diagram supports, in one line |
| **Data** | the numbers, or a pasted table / CSV (10 rows or fewer) |
| **Threshold** | the line, its unit, and where it came from: code, precedent, client, physics, or my guess |
| **Audience** | who looks at it, and for how long (e.g. client, 30 s) |
| **Must show** | the one thing the reader must see at a glance |

[If you cannot write the threshold line, that *is* your finding for this week. Bring it anyway.]{.ask-room}

[Write a recommendation for this site that is true under all four lines. Is a threshold just a number, or a number plus a counting rule?]{.ask-room}

## 1854: Snow drew a walking-distance line

[Old figures, read for their lines]{.kicker}

::: {.vibe-case}
::: {.vibe-visual}
![John Snow's cholera map of Soho, 1854. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.](../assets/anecdotes/snow-cholera-map.jpg)
:::
::: {.vibe-panel}
::: {.example-card}
[Threshold in the picture]{.card-title}
In a later version made for the parish inquiry (not the one shown), Snow added a dotted boundary: the points that were **equally far on foot** from the Broad Street pump and from the next nearest pump. The deaths sat inside the line.
:::

[Snow's boundary followed streets, not a circle. Compare it with the ring on our map two slides back.]{.ask-room}
:::
:::

---

## 1858: Nightingale made the comparison the line

::: {.vibe-case}
::: {.vibe-visual}
![Florence Nightingale's rose / coxcomb diagram of army mortality, 1858. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.](../assets/anecdotes/nightingale-rose.jpg)
:::
::: {.vibe-panel}
::: {.example-card}
[Threshold in the picture]{.card-title}
There is no number to clear. The line is relative: preventable disease against wounds. When the outer wedge dwarfs the inner one, the case is made.
:::

[Your threshold could be relative ("better than baseline by X") instead of absolute. Which would your audience trust more?]{.ask-room}
:::
:::

---

## 1869: Minard put the cold on its own axis

::: {.vibe-case}
::: {.vibe-visual}
![Charles Minard's figurative map of Napoleon's 1812 Russian campaign. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.](../assets/anecdotes/minard-napoleon.png)
:::
::: {.vibe-panel}
::: {.example-card}
[Threshold in the picture]{.card-title}
The temperature line along the bottom is tied to the shrinking army above it. You can see the band collapse as the cold drops. Challenger's charts were missing exactly this axis.
:::

[What is the "temperature line" in your project: the variable that, once it crosses a value, changes everything?]{.ask-room}
:::
:::

```{=html}
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="216" height="170" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--rule-soft)"/>
    <line x1="16" y1="30" x2="200" y2="30" stroke="var(--role-activity)" stroke-width="3"/>
    <line x1="16" y1="60" x2="200" y2="60" stroke="var(--role-activity)" stroke-width="3"/>
    <line x1="16" y1="118" x2="200" y2="118" stroke="var(--role-warn)" stroke-width="3"/>
    <line x1="16" y1="145" x2="200" y2="145" stroke="var(--role-warn)" stroke-width="3"/>
    <circle cx="108" cy="88" r="9" fill="var(--signal)"/>
    <text x="108" y="200" font-size="19" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--ink)">Ladder of lines</text>
    <text x="108" y="224" font-size="15" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--muted)">competing standards</text>
  </g>
  <g transform="translate(984,0)">
    <rect x="0" y="0" width="216" height="170" fill="#fff" stroke="var(--rule-soft)"/>

```
:::

Every pattern draws the line *inside* the figure. A threshold that only appears in a caption is a threshold the reader will miss.

[Which pattern fits your brief? Is there a sixth one we have not drawn?]{.ask-room}

## Your brief, drawn by someone else, three ways

[Session 2 · Swap studio]{.kicker}

::: {.spine-rail}
[Decision]{.node} [Evidence]{.node} [Variation]{.node} [Output]{.node} [Threshold]{.node .is-current} [Action]{.node}
:::

**Swap ring:** Student 1 → Student 2 → Instructor → Student 1. You draw the **Brief 1** of the next person in the ring, and your own brief comes back to you drawn three ways. If another student attends, they join the ring.

::: {.three-step}
::: {.step-box}
**1 · By hand · 8 min**

Paper and two pens: black plus one colour for the line. No software. Sketch fast, but the threshold must be drawn in.
:::
::: {.step-box}
**2 · With AI · 10 min**

Any chat or image tool. Paste the brief. Save the prompt and every output, including the bad ones.
:::
::: {.step-box}
**3 · From the data · 10 min**

Spreadsheet chart, the Threshold Explorer, or AI-written Python **that you run**. The numbers must come from the brief.
:::
:::

[Brief 2 goes round the ring in reverse as the exit task: one route of your choice.]{.feeds-tag}

## Prompt starter for round 2

::: {.concept-card}
[Paste into any AI tool, then paste your brief]{.card-title}
"You are drawing a decision diagram for an architecture audience. Draw **one** figure in which the threshold is a visible line or band inside the plot, the options are labelled directly (no legend), and the title states the takeaway. Use **only** the numbers in my brief. If you need a number that is not there, ask me. If you can, give me Python/matplotlib code instead of an image."
:::

:::: {.two-col}
::: {.warning-card}
[Image generators draw pictures *of* charts]{.card-title}
They can invent ticks, nudge the line, or round 48.4 down to "under 48". Fine for a layout sketch, but never as evidence.
:::
::: {.concept-card}
[Code is checkable]{.card-title}
A chart made by code you ran is a Week 8 "workflow/code" output: run it, check the units, and test it with one known value.
:::
::::

## Compare: lay out all nine

Put every drawing in Slack. **The brief's author** judges their own three versions; everyone else adds one note.

| Check | Hand | AI | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| **3-second test:** can you tell what's compared and who wins? | | | |
| Is the **threshold drawn** at the right value, in the right unit? | | | |
| Is **uncertainty** visible (band, range, confidence)? | | | |
| Did anything get **invented** (numbers, options, labels)? | | | |
| Which **one** goes on your object card, and what would you steal from the others? | | | |

[Which route told the story best, and was it the same route that got the numbers right?]{.ask-room}

## Defend one line (5 min each)

Each author takes one threshold from their winning diagram. The other two each take one role and attack it once. Rotate roles each round so everyone plays all three.

:::: {.two-col}

[Roles]{.card-title}

- **Client:** "That line costs me money."
- **Occupant:** "That line leaves me out."
- **Regulator:** "Where did that number come from?"

[Author answers with three things]{.card-title}

1. the source: code, precedent, client, physics, or my guess
2. how far it can move before the recommendation flips
3. what evidence would make you move it

## The sentence that goes on the card

::: {.concept-card}
[Recommendation sentence, Week 9 version]{.card-title}
**For [audience], I recommend [option] because it clears [threshold] ([source]). This changes if [threshold] moves by [how much] or if [counter-argument] holds.**
:::

::: {.example-card}
[Worked from today's facade data]{.card-title}
For the client team, I recommend **Hybrid** because it passes all five thresholds in our Week 3 matrix. This changes to **Deep fins** if the solar gain line tightens by about 19% (to ≤ 38.9) or the depth allowance drops below about 0.62 m.
:::

## Reconstruct your threshold diagram in four steps

**Object this week: the diagram of your own brief that you chose, and the line inside it.**

::: {.recall-4step}
::: {.step}
**Did** Which version did you choose (hand, AI, or data), and what is its one message?
:::
::: {.step}
**Assumed** Where does the line come from, and who chose it?
:::
::: {.step}
**Risk** How far can it move before the recommendation flips? What did AI get wrong?
:::
::: {.step}
**Verify** Which number in the figure did you check against the brief?
:::
:::
